$comment: The SHARED lifecycle-pointer fixture corpus. Copied BYTE-IDENTICALLY into every repository that implements the pointer grammar (this marketplace's scripts/lifecycle_pointers.py and Roubo's shared/lifecycle-resolver.ts). What is SHARED is the grammar: `expected` is the result of splitting the pointer, and every runner asserts it. What is NOT shared is `marketplace_only`, which records this repository's link-checking outcome; Roubo resolves gate reachability instead and ignores that block. See lifecycle-pointer-fixtures.md for the schema, the copy contract, and which side is authoritative on disagreement. Do NOT add a case here without adding a runner assertion on BOTH sides.

fixtures.name: bare-pointer-resolves-in-the-owning-spec
fixtures.note: A pointer with no colon names a case in THIS spec.

fixtures.name: bare-pointer-naming-a-case-the-owning-spec-does-not-have
fixtures.note: The owning spec is the target; the case id is absent, so the pointer dangles.

fixtures.name: bare-pointer-is-never-resolved-against-a-sibling-spec
fixtures.note: A same-id case in another spec must NOT rescue a bare pointer.

fixtures.name: slug-qualified-pointer-resolves-cross-spec
fixtures.note: The first colon splits slug from case id.

fixtures.name: target-spec-carrying-no-cases-reads-as-a-missing-case
fixtures.note: `null` means the folder exists with no test-cases.json at all: the folder resolves, the case does not.

fixtures.name: split-is-on-the-first-colon-so-a-colon-inside-the-case-id-survives
fixtures.note: Never split on the last colon, never on every colon.

fixtures.name: empty-pointer-splits-to-an-empty-case-id-in-the-owning-spec
fixtures.note: GRAMMAR only: with no colon the owning slug carries an empty case id. Whether that is its own outcome is per-implementation. This marketplace reports `empty pointer`; Roubo's schema rejects an empty replacement outright (z.string().min(1)), so the input never reaches its resolver in production.

fixtures.name: spec-level-supersession-is-never-walked-as-a-case-pointer
fixtures.note: `legacy` is superseded by `current`, and `current` HAS TC-050, but a bare case pointer still splits against `legacy` and is never redirected. Roubo agrees on the split and reports its own `target archived` outcome, which is why the outcome half is marketplace-only.

fixtures.name: spec-level-supersession-does-not-redirect-a-slug-qualified-pointer
fixtures.note: Pointing at the archived spec splits to the archived spec, not to its successor.

fixtures.name: a-pointer-into-an-archived-spec-splits-against-that-spec
fixtures.note: Archived is not unreachable to the GRAMMAR. This marketplace then resolves it against that spec's own cases and finds TC-050; Roubo fails it closed as `target archived`, because it is answering whether a gate obligation transfers. The split is the shared part.
